newsitem.title: UK: Britons aim to re-enact Newfoundland's discovery.
newsitem.headline: Britons aim to re-enact Newfoundland's discovery.

text.p: Nineteen mariners plan to set sail next year in a replica of a 15th century ship to repeat the historic voyage in which explorer John Cabot discovered the island of Newfoundland.
British brewers Courage announced on Thursday they were contributing 100,000 pounds ($167,000) towards the venture.
The replica, named the Matthew after Cabot's vessel, will leave Bristol on May 2 -- 500 years to the day after the Venetian adventurer set off from the western England port.
Captain David Alan-Williams said his crew will sleep on mattresses on the floor of the 40-tonne bunkless craft.
Cabot, whose real name was Giovanni Caboto, sailed from Bristol looking for a passage to Asia after visiting Mecca and seeing the eastern spices, perfumes, silks and precious stones traded there.

Rejected by Spain and Portugal, Cabot sought support from England's Henry VII. Historians say Henry's backing may have been the factor which determined that North America was colonised by English rather than the Spanish or Portuguese.
Cabot took 52 days to reach Newfoundland. On the way, he discovered the world's richest fishing grounds off the Grand Banks.
